title: Catalog binding models and CRUD guide
content:
Summary

This note sketches a pragmatic data model for the control plane catalog (resources, environments, regions, clusters) and a set of CRUD API conventions that work across multi-region deployments and heterogeneous routing policies. Focus is on clear ownership boundaries, idempotent operations, predictable read paths, and safe fanout for writes to region controllers.

Goals and constraints
- Single global source of truth for resource metadata and routing intent.
- Low-latency route decision for the runtime (local caches, materialized indices).
- Safe, idempotent CRUD with conflict semantics that are easy for clients.
- Support strong per-tenant isolation (namespaces + binding scoping).
- Allow eventual consistency for cross-region replication while providing mechanisms for fast reconciliation.

Key entities (conceptual)
- CatalogResource: logical object representing something the platform serves (model, model-variant, endpoint, batch-queue). Immutable identity + mutable spec + lifecycle metadata.
  - id: uuid (global)
  - owner_id: org/team
  - logical_name: stable human slug (namespace-scoped)
  - spec: opaque JSON blob (typed per resource kind)
  - resource_version: opaque token (monotonic, used for optimistic concurrency)
  - lifecycle_state: provisioning | active | draining | decommissioned
  - bindings: list of BindingRef (optional short form)

- Environment: lightweight grouping (dev/stage/prod) used for routing policy inheritance.
  - id, name, elevated_policies, org_scope

- Region: physical/geographic region identifier (us-west1, eu-central1). Region records include capability tags (gpu-types, network-accelerated, private-network-only).

- Cluster: a logical cluster within a region that can host workloads. Clusters expose capacity, feature flags, and current availability metrics emitted by SRE agents.

- Binding (Control-plane binding): declarative assignment that maps a CatalogResource to one or more ClusterRefs with placement policy and weight. Binding is the unit of routing intent that controllers reconcile into cluster-local routes.
  - id, resource_id, env_id, region_constraints, cluster_candidates, selected_cluster (nullable), policy, last_applied_version

Identifier and namespacing rules
- Global UUIDs are the canonical identifiers for programmatic APIs.
- User-facing names are namespace-scoped: /org/{org}/env/{env}/resources/{slug}. Slugs must be stable and unique within an env.
- Clients may supply a client-generated idempotency key for create operations.

Versioning and concurrency
- Every mutable entity has a resource_version (string) produced by the control plane on update. Clients use If-Match: resource_version for conditional updates.
- For cross-region replication, writes are accepted at the control plane master, which returns the new resource_version. Region controllers subscribe to a change-feed and apply deltas.
- For bulk or automated changes, we support server-side retries with deterministic merge hooks. Complex merges should be performed by the control plane API (PATCH with a merge strategy parameter).

CRUD API conventions (summary)
Base: POST /v1/orgs/{org}/resources  -- create
GET /v1/orgs/{org}/resources/{id} -- read
PATCH /v1/orgs/{org}/resources/{id} -- partial update (merge semantics)
PUT /v1/orgs/{org}/resources/{id} -- upsert (replace semantics)
DELETE /v1/orgs/{org}/resources/{id} -- delete (soft-delete by default)
LIST /v1/orgs/{org}/envs/{env}/resources -- list scoped by env with filter query params

Create semantics
- Idempotency: client may send Idempotency-Key header. If the key is seen, return the original resource.
- Server assigns canonical id if not provided. Creation validates quotas and owner scoping synchronously.
- Response includes Location header and the created resource representation with resource_version.

Update semantics
- PATCH is the preferred operation for most clients. PATCH default: shallow merge for top-level fields, merge-array-by-key for arrays annotated with keys. PATCH supports query param ?mergeStrategy=replaceArrays to change behavior.
- PUT replaces the spec entirely and requires If-Match header to avoid accidental replacement.
- Conflicts return 409 with the latest representation and a short explanation. Clients are encouraged to re-read and reapply.

Delete semantics
- Soft-delete: set lifecycle_state=decommissioning and mark deletion_ts. A background reconciler finalizes removal when bindings are drained.
- Immediate hard delete is only allowed for resources in provisioning failures or by admins.

Read and listing patterns
- Consistency levels: clients can request ?consistency=strong|stale|cached. Strong reads are routed to the control-plane master; cached reads come from materialized indices in the serving plane (low latency).
- List endpoints support efficient pagination and filter by region/cluster/capability tag so routing decisions can be made without fetching full spec for every item.

Routing policy model (how binding intent is expressed)
- Policy primitives: prefer_local, minimize_cost, meet_latency_slo, capability_filter, pin_to_clusters, failover_order.
- Policies are composable and evaluate to a ranked list of candidate clusters.
- Inheritance: org-level -> env-level -> resource-level. Resource-level settings override.
- Example: a model resource can have policy = { "prefer_local": true, "capability_filter": ["a100","sparse-kernels"], "failover_order": ["reserved-gpus","shared-gpus"] }

Cluster selection lifecycle
1) Control-plane evaluates binding policy and emits binding record with selected_cluster candidates + score metadata.
2) Region controller reconciler watches binding records and attempts to claim capacity on the chosen cluster.
3) If claim fails (capacity or health), controller marks a binding failure and control-plane re-evaluates alternatives (backoff with jitter).
4) When cluster is selected and routes are provisioned, serving layer notes the active binding and readiness is reported in CatalogResource.status.

Fanout and multi-region safety
- Writes to the control plane are authoritative. Controllers in each region pull change events. We avoid synchronous fanout across region control planes to keep write latency bounded.
- To reduce stale reads, the control plane maintains a small per-org high-water mark index (hot-index) that mirrors binding decisions and cluster assignments; this index is replicated with low-latency pub/sub. It is optimized for route lookups, not full spec materialization.

Edge cases and operational considerations
- Partial failures: if region controller A has applied a binding but B hasn't, we treat the binding as _tentative_ until majority or readiness checkpoint. Tentative bindings are not returned for strong route decisions.
- Reconciler idempotency: controllers should use update-if-unmodified semantics using resource_version from binding records.
- Schema evolution: specs include a schema_version and a typed descriptor. Controllers should tolerate unknown fields and ignore them rather than failing.

Audit, security, and tenant isolation
- Every write is logged with actor, ip, and idempotency-key.
- RBAC: operations are scoped by org id and elevated roles required for cross-org operations.
- KMS-wrapped secrets inside specs are stored encrypted; control plane never expands them in logs.

Examples (short)
- Create resource (client supplies slug): POST /v1/orgs/acme/resources Body: { "slug": "summarizer-v2", "spec": {"model":"open-xxl","quant":"q8"}, "env": "prod" }
  Response: 201 Location: /v1/orgs/acme/resources/uuid-123 Body: {"id":"uuid-123","slug":"summarizer-v2","spec":{...},"resource_version":"rv-457"} 

- Patch binding (conditional): PATCH /v1/orgs/acme/bindings/{bind-id} Headers: If-Match: rv-457 Body: {"policy":{"prefer_local":true, "min_capacity":2}}
  If resource_version mismatches, server returns 409 with latest.

Operational notes and TODOs
- Define exact resource_version format (monotonic int vs vector clock) — current leaning: a composite token [epoch]-[monotonic] per org to keep single-master semantics but allow easy comparison.
- Implement server-side dry-run mode for destructive PATCH/DELETE so client UIs can preview effects.
- Add deterministic merge functions for commonly mutated fields (bindings array, cluster_candidates).
- Create a lightweight read-only materialized view for the serving runtime tuned to fast route lookup queries (index: resource_id + env + region + capability_tags).

Appendix: quick glossary
- hot-index: small replicated index curated for fast route decision reads.
- binding: control-plane object expressing placement intent for a resource in an env/region.
- tentative binding: binding in the middle of cluster-claiming flows, not yet considered active.
- resource_version: optimistic concurrency token attached to mutable objects.

Notes to reviewers
- Looking for feedback on: idempotency model (client-key vs server-generated), resource_version format, and expected failover latency targets for re-evaluating bindings after a cluster failure.

End of doc
